introduction: On this first Sunday of Lent, God makes a covenant with Noah and every living creature, and sets the rainbow in the clouds as its sign. Peter sees in the waters of the flood a sign of Baptism, which now saves us. Mark tells us that the Spirit drove Jesus into the wilderness for forty days, where he was tempted and the angels served him. Today, in many dioceses, catechumens are presented to the bishop as they prepare for Baptism at Easter. Let us walk with them through the desert toward the joy of the Resurrection.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, God remembers his covenant with us and every living creature. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church in this holy season: that she may follow Christ into the desert of Lent and come out renewed in faith and love. Let us pray to the Lord.
For catechumens and those preparing to enter full communion with the Church: that they may be strengthened by our prayers and example on their way to Easter. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who are tempted, tested, or tired: that, like Jesus in the wilderness, they may find strength in God and be served by his angels. Let us pray to the Lord.
For our common home and every living creature: that we may care for the earth God has entrusted to us. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may renew the grace of our Baptism this Lent, turning from sin and believing in the Good News. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Faithful God, you never forget your covenant. Strengthen us in this time of testing, keep us faithful to our Baptism, and bring us to the joy of Easter. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: The desert and the rainbow
reflection.body:
After the flood, God speaks to Noah and makes a promise that reaches every creature: "There will never again be a flood to destroy the earth." As a sign, he says, "I set my rainbow in the cloud." Notice who remembers: "I will remember my covenant." Lent begins not with our effort but with God's faithfulness.

Peter connects that story with our own. In Noah's ship "few, that is, eight souls, were saved through water," and he writes: "This is a symbol of baptism, which now saves you." Lent is a season to remember our Baptism, and for catechumens, to prepare for theirs.

Mark's account of the temptation is very short. "Immediately the Spirit drove him out into the wilderness. He was there in the wilderness forty days, tempted by Satan." Mark adds a detail the other Gospels leave out: "He was with the wild animals; and the angels were serving him." The desert is a place of danger and of grace at the same time. Jesus faces temptation, and he is not left alone.

Then he comes out to preach: "The time is fulfilled, and God's Kingdom is at hand! Repent, and believe in the Good News." The forty days in the wilderness are not an end in themselves. They prepare for a mission.

Our Lent is a small desert of forty days. We will meet temptation there, but we will also meet the Spirit who leads us and the grace that serves us. This week, pray the psalm of today's liturgy each morning: "Show me your ways, LORD. Teach me your paths." And if you know someone preparing for Baptism or Confirmation at Easter, pray for them by name.
